content.title: About
content.content: Canned potato (NS) is boiled potatoes packed in airtight cans with added salt and sometimes spices. The product retains a soft texture and characteristic flavor, suitable for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows potatoes to be stored for 2‑3 years without loss of taste.
Cans usually contain low‑starch potato varieties to keep the pieces intact during heat treatment.
NS stands for “not salty”, meaning the product has a moderate salt level.
Canned potatoes are often used in military rations and backpacking meals.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B6, which supports protein metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Helps maintain fluid‑electrolyte balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber aids digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned potatoes contain virtually no fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Even with the NS label, some salt is present; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Bisphenol A
items.content: Older cans may be lined with BPA‑containing coating; choose products in modern packaging.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If a can is damaged, bacterial growth is possible, so always check the integrity of the packaging.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned potatoes can be eaten cold in salads, heated in the microwave, added to soups, stews, or mashed. After opening, drain the brine and optionally season with fresh herbs or spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, transfer the contents to an airtight container and keep refrigerated, using within 2‑3 days.
